title: Stop provider output after a duplicate tool-call flood
hypothesis: Stopping a Codex stream after its third duplicate complete valid tool call will preserve the unique executable prefix while reducing response size and long-tail latency.
falsified_if: The cutoff causes any new deterministic failure or materially increases model/tool calls, response size, or latency because useful unique calls commonly arrive after the duplicate threshold.
local_evidence: Raw LCA eval transcripts contained 19-24 duplicate calls on tiny edit tasks even though the core later discarded them.
decision_rule: Reject on any new deterministic correctness, concurrent-change, or scope failure. Otherwise adopt only if capped runs reduce transcript-derived response size or upper-tail latency without materially increasing model/tool calls. Provider token totals are diagnostic only because an intentional cutoff can omit the final usage event.
